citation: William H. Rau, 'President Roosevelt in his carriage after dedication of Philadelphia High School', stereograph, copyright 1902 (card no. X4903, the date in the handwritten caption ending '-02'). Library of Congress, Prints and Photographs Division, Stereograph Cards, LC-DIG-stereo-1s01985 (item 2010647266).
repository: Library of Congress, Prints and Photographs Division. Master TIFF 1s01985u.tif (5034 x 2572), read at tile.loc.gov; the left-hand frame and a crop of the coachman are kept in kevinrhaas/chicago-evidence evidence/people-references-2026-11-06/coachman_1904/.
locator: The left-hand frame of the card: a closed carriage at the kerb, its coachman on the box seen from his right side at a few metres, Roosevelt and a companion in the body, a mounted hussar of the escort behind.
rights_note: LOC rights advisory: 'No known restrictions on publication.' Published 1902. Used only as a reference picture people are judged against (T-3417); nothing is traced or sampled from it.
access_notes: Viewed 2026-11-06 (T-3417) from the master TIFF. The coachman sits upright on a cushioned box with his knees high and his feet on the footboard; a full-length box coat, single-breasted with large flat buttons, falls over his thighs and hangs down past the seat in heavy folds; a stand-fall collar with a white stock above; a tall silk hat with a curled brim; reins and whip gathered in the right hand at his lap. Not Chicago (Philadelphia), but the same role, class of carriage and decade as the 1904 scene's coachman.
note: One of the 1904 coachman reference set's photographs (data/humans/reference_sets/coachman_1904.json).
